title: Un tinto antes del aguacero en Bogotá

dialogue.speaker: Natalia
dialogue.spanish: Uy, Andrés, mirá esas nubes negras sobre los cerros de Monserrate. Se va a venir un aguacero tenaz.
dialogue.english: Whoa, Andrés, look at those dark clouds over the Monserrate hills. A fierce downpour is about to hit.

slang.actualMeaning: intense / fierce / crazy (very common Bogotá slang)
slang.example: El tráfico por la Séptima hoy está tenaz.

dialogue.speaker: Andrés
dialogue.spanish: Pues sí, qué frío tan berraco y ninguno de los dos trajo sombrilla hoy.
dialogue.english: Well yeah, it's freezing cold and neither of us brought an umbrella today.

dialogue.speaker: Natalia
dialogue.spanish: Bueno, entremos rápido a esta cafetería de la esquina y nos tomamos un tinto bien caliente.
dialogue.english: Well, let's duck quickly into this corner café and have a piping hot black coffee.

slang.actualMeaning: a cup of black coffee (in Colombia, 'tinto' means black coffee, not red wine!)
slang.example: ¿Me regala un tinto sin azúcar, por favor?

dialogue.speaker: Andrés
dialogue.spanish: Buena idea. O sea, aprovechamos para pedir dos almojábanas recién salidas del horno mientras escampa.
dialogue.english: Good idea. I mean, let's take the chance to order two cheese breads fresh out of the oven while the rain stops.

dialogue.speaker: Natalia
dialogue.spanish: Sí, el señor dice que cada combo de tinto con almojábana cuesta seis mil pesos.
dialogue.english: Yes, the man says each combo of black coffee with cheese bread costs six thousand pesos.

dialogue.speaker: Andrés
dialogue.spanish: Listo, de una. Apenas pare la lluvia caminamos dos cuadras a la estación de TransMilenio.
dialogue.english: Done, let's do it. As soon as the rain stops we'll walk two blocks to the TransMilenio bus station.

slang.actualMeaning: right away / let's do it / count me in

questions.question: Why do Natalia and Andrés decide to duck into a café in Bogotá?
options: It's freezing cold, neither brought an umbrella, and a fierce rainstorm ('aguacero') is coming
They have a business meeting with a client there
Andrés needs Wi-Fi to send an email
questions.explanation: Natalia sees dark clouds ('se va a venir un aguacero tenaz') and Andrés notes neither of them brought an umbrella.

questions.question: What food do they order with their coffee, and how much is each combo?
options: Warm cheese breads ('almojábanas') for 6,000 pesos per combo
questions.explanation: They order 'dos almojábanas recién salidas del horno' and Natalia says each combo costs 6,000 pesos.

questions.question: What is their plan once the rain stops ('mientras escampa')?
options: Walk two blocks to the TransMilenio bus station
Call a taxi to go to the airport
questions.explanation: Andrés says: 'Apenas pare la lluvia caminamos dos cuadras a la estación de TransMilenio.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: When Natalia orders 'un tinto bien caliente' in Colombia, what is she ordering?
options: A cup of hot black coffee (not red wine!)
A glass of mulled red wine
A cup of hot chocolate with cheese
questions.explanation: False-friend alert! In Colombia, 'un tinto' always means a small cup of black coffee, whereas in Spain 'vino tinto' is red wine.
